property_summary: When caller is the owner who has not been approved as a logger, the reference returns false from approvedToLog(owner) while the bug also returns false, but I need a case where they differ: if the owner first calls setApprovedLogger(owner, true) to become approved, then the reference returns true for approvedToLog(owner) but the bug (returning false) still returns false, causing the assertion that the reference's return is true to fail on the buggy contract.
After the owner sets themselves as an approved logger via setApprovedLogger(owner, true), the reference returns true from approvedToLog(owner) while the bug returns false.
Owner sets themselves as approved logger, then the reference approvedToLog returns true while the bug returns false.

After the owner sets themselves as an approved logger via setApprovedLogger(owner, true), the reference returns true from approvedToLog(owner) while the buggy version (which always returns false) returns false, causing the assertion that approvedToLog(owner) is true to fail on the buggy contract.
After owner sets themselves as an approved logger, reference returns true from approvedToLog(owner) while buggy version returns false.
After owner calls setApprovedLogger(alice, true), reading approvedLoggers(alice) returns true in reference but false in mutant because mutant always stores false.

After owner sets approvedLogger for alice to true and for bob to false, bob calls approvedToLog(bob) which should return false in reference (because bob is not approved) but fails assertion because the test instead checks a different fact not relying on the bug; here we test that after setApprovedLogger(alice, true), approvedLoggers(alice) returns true in reference but false in mutant.
After owner calls setApprovedLogger(alice, true), reading approvedLoggers(alice) returns true in reference but false in mutant because mutant always stores false.

After owner calls setApprovedLogger(alice, true) and then alice calls logFunded(), the reference emits Funded event and returns true, while the buggy version returns false because approvedLoggers[alice] is always set to false.
After owner calls setApprovedLogger(alice, false), reading approvedLoggers(alice) returns false in reference but true in mutant because mutant always stores false regardless of _status.
After the owner calls setApprovedLogger(alice, false), alice is approved in the mutant but not in the reference; calling approvedToLog(alice) returns true for M but false for P.

After owner calls setApprovedLogger(alice, true) then setApprovedLogger(bob, false), bob is approved in the mutant but not in the reference; calling c.approvedLoggers(bob) returns true for M but false for P.

Owner sets alice's approval to false, then bob calls approvedToLog; in reference bob returns false (not approved), but in mutant bob returns true (because logger was set to true regardless of _status).
After owner calls setApprovedLogger(alice, false), alice is approved in the mutant but not in the reference; reading c.approvedLoggers(alice) returns true for M but false for P.
After owner calls setApprovedLogger(alice, true) then setApprovedLogger(alice, false), reading c.approvedLoggers(alice) returns false for the reference (correct) and true for the mutant (bug).

After the owner sets `approvedLoggers[alice] = true` and then sets it back to `false`, only the reference contract respects the revocation; the mutated contract (with the always-pass `onlyOwner`) ignores the `onlyOwner` check in `setApprovedLogger` and thus the state of `approvedLoggers` for an unprivileged caller becomes inconsistently true.

After the owner sets approvedLoggers[alice]=true and then a non-owner attempts to set it back to false, only the reference contract reverts the change; the mutated contract allows any caller to modify approvedLoggers, so the mapping differs for key alice.

After the owner sets approvedLoggers[alice]=true and then a non-owner (bob) calls setApprovedLogger(alice, false), the reference contract reverts (preserving approvedLoggers[alice]=true) while the buggy contract silently succeeds (setting approvedLoggers[alice]=false), causing the value of approvedLoggers[alice] to differ.

After owner sets approvedLoggers[alice]=true, then a non-owner (bob) calls setApprovedLogger(alice, false): reference contract reverts (preserving true), buggy contract succeeds (setting false), causing approvedLoggers(alice) to diverge.

After owner sets approvedLoggers[alice]=true, then a non-owner (bob) calls setApprovedLogger(alice, false): reference contract reverts (preserving true) while buggy contract succeeds (setting false), causing approvedLoggers(alice) to diverge.

After a non-owner calls setApprovedLogger to approve themselves, the reference contract's approvedToLog returns false (because owner-only modifier was removed in the bug), while the buggy version returns true.

After a non-owner calls setApprovedLogger to approve themselves, the reference contract's approvedToLog returns false (because owner-only modifier reverts in the reference), while the buggy version returns true.

After a non-owner (address(0x1)) calls setApprovedLogger(address(0x1), true), the reference contract (which requires owner) does not log them, so approvedToLog(address(0x1)) returns false; the buggy contract (which allows any caller) logs them, so approvedToLog(address(0x1)) returns true.

After a non-owner calls setApprovedLogger to approve themselves, the reference contract (with onlyOwner modifier) does not change the logger's status, so approvedToLog returns false; the buggy contract (without modifier) allows the change, so approvedToLog returns true.

After a non-owner (address 0x1) calls setApprovedLogger to approve themselves, the reference contract (with onlyOwner modifier) reverts, so approvedToLog returns false; the buggy contract (without modifier) approves them, so approvedToLog returns true.
When an unapproved logger calls logRedemptionRequested, the reference returns true (emits event) while the bug returns false (no emit).
After setting an approved logger, a call to logRedemptionRequested from that logger returns true in the reference but false in the bug.

After an unapproved logger directly invokes logRedemptionRequested, the reference reverts (because onlyOwner check is missing, but the function returns false due to !approvedToLog) while the bug returns false (approvedToLog is false, so returns false without reverting); the test asserts that the call does NOT revert in both, but the bug returns false while reference also returns false — actually both return false, not diverging. However, the difference is that the reference requires the caller to be the owner to set approved loggers, so an unapproved logger can never become approved; the bug in logRedemptionRequested returns false for non-approved callers, same as reference. Actually the only divergence is when an approved logger calls: reference returns true and emits event, bug returns false and does not emit event. But that was already tried. Therefore, no new concrete scenario works — the property must be that after setting an approved logger, a call from that logger returns true in reference and false in bug, but that's already stated as tried. So I'll craft a test where an approved logger calls logRedemptionRequested: reference returns true, bug returns false, asserting the return value via try/catch.
After setting an approved logger and having that approved logger call logRedemptionRequested, the reference returns true (emits event) while the bug returns false (no emit).
After the owner sets an approved logger, that logger calls logRedemptionRequested; the reference returns true (emits the event), while the buggy version returns false (does not emit).
After setting an approved logger, calling logRedemptionRequested returns true in the reference but false in the mutant (change of return value from true to false).
After the owner sets caller as an approved logger, logRedemptionRequested returns true on the reference but false on the mutant.
When caller is approved, reference logRegisteredPubkey returns true but buggy version returns false, so approval check after the call returns incorrectly.
When an approved logger calls logRegisteredPubkey, the reference returns true but the buggy version returns false.
After the owner sets a caller as approved logger, calling logRegisteredPubkey returns true on reference but false on buggy version, observed via a direct return value check.

When an approved logger calls logRegisteredPubkey after being set by the owner, the reference returns true but the buggy version returns false, observable via a direct return value check from c.logRegisteredPubkey.
After owner sets address(1) as approved logger, calling logRegisteredPubkey returns true on reference but false on buggy version, detected by comparing return value.
When an approved logger calls logRegisteredPubkey, the reference returns true while the buggy version returns false.
When a caller that is NOT an approved logger calls logRegisteredPubkey, the reference returns true, but the mutant reverts.
When an approved logger calls logRegisteredPubkey, the reference returns true, but the mutant reverts.
When an approved logger calls logRegisteredPubkey, the reference returns true but the mutant reverts, causing an observable divergence in the return value.
When an approved logger calls logRegisteredPubkey, the reference returns true but the buggy mutant reverts, causing an observable divergence via try/catch around the call.
When a non-approved logger calls logRegisteredPubkey, the reference returns true but the buggy mutant reverts, observable via try/catch.
Call logSetupFailed from an approved logger and check that the approved logger reverts (false) in correct contract and does not revert (true) in buggy contract.

For an unapproved caller, logSetupFailed returns true (non-revert) in the reference but false (revert due to the condition) in the buggy version, so after calling logSetupFailed from an unapproved logger, asserting that the return value is true passes on reference but fails on buggy.

When an unapproved caller calls logSetupFailed, the reference returns true (no revert) whereas the buggy version returns false (revert because it checks that caller IS approved), so asserting that the return value is true passes on reference and fails on buggy.

When an unapproved caller calls logSetupFailed, the reference contract returns true (emits event), while the buggy contract returns false (due to flipping the condition), so asserting that logSetupFailed returns true passes on the reference but fails on the buggy version.
When an approved logger calls logSetupFailed, the reference returns true but the buggy version returns false because the condition is flipped.
When an approved logger calls logFraudDuringSetup, the reference contract returns true while the buggy contract returns false.
After the owner sets an address as an approved logger, that approved address calls logFraudDuringSetup: the reference returns true, the buggy version returns false.
When non-owner address is set as approved logger, calling logFraudDuringSetup returns true in reference but false in buggy version.
After the owner sets a random address as an approved logger, calling logFraudDuringSetup from that address returns true in the reference but false in the buggy version.
When owner sets address(0x1) as approved logger, then address(0x1) calls logFraudDuringSetup, reference returns true, buggy returns false.

When a non-approved logger calls logStartedLiquidation(false), the reference returns true (since it checks approvedToLog(msg.sender) and finds it false, so it proceeds to emit and return true), while the bug inverts the condition and returns false without emitting.
When an approved logger calls logStartedLiquidation, the reference emits and returns true, while the bug inverts the condition, returning false without emitting.

When the owner calls setApprovedLogger(address(this), false) and then calls logStartedLiquidation(false) as address(this), the reference returns true (since the caller is not approved), while the bug inverts the condition and returns false.
When a non-approved logger calls logStartedLiquidation(true), the reference contract returns true while the buggy contract returns false.

When a non-approved caller (address(0x1)) invokes logStartedLiquidation(false), the reference returns true (since the check approvedToLog(msg.sender) is false and the condition proceeds to emit), while the buggy version inverts the check and returns false.
After setting an approved logger, calling logRedeemed with a specific txid returns true in the reference but false in the mutant.
After setting an approved logger, logRedeemed returns true in the reference but false in the mutant.
After an approved logger calls logRedeemed with bytes32(0x1234), the reference returns true, but the mutant returns false.
Approved logger calls logRedeemed with bytes32(uint256(0x1234)), reference returns true, mutant returns false.
After setting an approved logger, calling logRedeemed with bytes32(0x0) returns true in the reference but false in the mutant.
After approving an address as a logger, calling logLiquidated() from that address returns true in the reference contract and false in the buggy contract.
When a caller not approved to log calls logExitedCourtesyCall, the reference contract returns true (after emitting) while the buggy contract returns false.
When an approved logger calls logExitedCourtesyCall, the reference returns true while the buggy version returns false.
An approved logger calls logExitedCourtesyCall(); the reference returns true, the bug returns false.
When an approved logger calls logExitedCourtesyCall(), the reference returns true while the buggy version returns false.
When an approved logger calls logExitedCourtesyCall(), the reference returns true while the buggy version returns false.
